searchText: Hello there! I'm reading Mastering Bitcoin book and in the first of the book that introduces parts of the blockchain , it mentions taht there are 2 types of nodes ( miners and block signers ). When it gets into details, again it mentions that a node starts a transaction by first creating it and then digitally signing it with its private key. I'm utterly confused regarding this statement. A TX is signed by a private key and the idea of the node is to verify if that's ok. Either I have a big gap in my knowledge / understanding or this statement in the book is wrong. Or... probably it talks about something else... I guess the EoA signs an intent of action and when that is received by the node then the node triggers a transaction and it signs the transaction with its private key... In Proof of Work, (Bitcoin and Ethereum previously) blocks are not signed. > miners and block signers You sure it doesn't say "miners and transaction signers"?
